Double fertilization involves two fusions. One male gamete fuses with the egg to form a diploid zygote ($2n$). The other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei in the central cell, forming a triploid primary endosperm nucleus ($3n$). The embryo sac, part of the female gametophyte, houses these processes.
Explain the process of double fertilization in plants, including the types of nuclei involved and their outcomes.

The relational model (proposed by E.F. Codd, 1970) organizes data into tables with rows and columns, where each table links to others through matching key values. This contrasts with hierarchical and network models which use tree and graph structures respectively. For a database to be in first normal form (1NF), every column must contain atomic values without repeating groups. Each row in a table represents an entity instance with distinct values across columns, ensuring data consistency and integrity within the DBMS.
Explain the concept of the relational model in database management systems as proposed by E.F. Codd in 1970, and describe what it means for a database to be in first normal form (1NF).
